text:
tanya: Observing a reproducible stall in the Python async SDK when our token rotation causes a burst of 401s. requests start queuing and never complete.
lee: can you share a minimal repro? sounds like pool/transport state isn't cleared on auth failure.
tanya: repro attached below. runs under uvloop + httpx. concurrency 60 and after token swap we see a big backlog.
tanya: repro steps:
```
# run repro
python examples/token_rotate_repro.py --clients 60 --interval 0.1
# then update token in vault to cause 401s for ~12s
```
tanya: logs: 
```
WARNING httpcore._backends.auto: Reusing closed transport (fd=56)
ERROR httpx._exceptions.ReadError: Unable to read from connection
ERROR asyncio: Task exception was never retrieved
```
omar: rough guess: transport gets reset during auth retry and is re-queued to pool as usable. next request grabs it and blocks.
lee: does our AsyncClient expose a way to mark a connection bad? I thought httpx allows `transport.close()` but pool might rewrap it.
nina: also found a typing issue: AsyncRedwoodClient.__aenter__ is typed as returning Any which makes mypy silent when users create a client at module scope and never close it. this hides misuse.
lee: workaround: explicitly set pool limits and shorter keepalive, or call `await client.aclose()` on token refresh. that forced-close cleared the backlog in our test.
omar: can confirm, calling aclose() on token rotation makes requests recover. but that's heavy-handed; we'd prefer pool-level eviction on auth errors.
tanya: stack trace snippet: 
```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpcore/_exceptions.py", line 32, in some
  raise ReadError("...") from exc
ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
# then pool logs: put connection back into available list
```
dev-bot: CI job queued: dexsdk/connpool-rotation-ci #17.
lee: plan: 1) make pool mark transports as unusable when a request fails due to auth/connection reset; 2) add an explicit `client.ensure_healthy()` helper and a `on_auth_error_drop` flag (default true) so auth-paths won't leave bad transports; 3) typing PR to tighten AsyncRedwoodClient context manager return type so mypy complains on unsafe patterns.
omar: runtime follow-up: we should also track metrics for "evicted_on_auth_error" and add a dashboard. helps correlate token-rotation incidents.
tanya: I'll open an SDK issue with logs + gist and attach the repro script. created #2451 with description and test notes.
lee: thanks. assigning to @omar for pool fix, @nina for typing PR, and will add a short docs blurb about token rotation best practices (call aclose() or use short-lived connections).
tanya: leaving here the gist link: https://gist.github.com/tanya/token-rotation-repro - will test the pool patch once ready. :thumbsup:
